invariants_created: OPTIONS can be sent at any time; does not change session state (INIT remains INIT)
DESCRIBE typically precedes SETUP but is not strictly required by the protocol
SETUP must precede PLAY, PAUSE, RECORD
PLAY requires prior SETUP (READY state); transitions to PLAYING state
PAUSE requires PLAYING state; transitions back to READY state
TEARDOWN terminates the session; can be sent from READY or PLAYING state; transitions to INIT
GET_PARAMETER can be sent at any time, including during PLAYING state
DESCRIBE may fail with 404 and be retried successfully
Session header is required in all requests after SETUP has been performed
CSeq header is mandatory in every request and response, monotonically increasing per method
Transport header is mandatory in SETUP request
RECORD transitions from READY to RECORDING state
REDIRECT is server-to-client only
ANNOUNCE can be client-to-server or server-to-client
ALL.CSeq: Mandatory in every request and response. Must be a monotonically increasing integer per method.
SETUP.Transport: Mandatory. Specifies transport protocol (RTP/UDP, RTP/TCP) and parameters including client_port, server_port, interleaved, multicast, unicast, etc.
PLAY.Session: Mandatory. Must contain the session identifier received from the SETUP response.
PAUSE.Session: Mandatory. Must contain the session identifier received from the SETUP response.
TEARDOWN.Session: Mandatory. Must contain the session identifier received from the SETUP response. Session becomes invalid after TEARDOWN.
RECORD.Session: Mandatory. Must contain the session identifier received from the SETUP response.
OPTIONS.Public: Response header listing all supported methods. Not present in request.
DESCRIBE.Accept: Recommended in request, typically application/sdp. Response Content-Type should match.
DESCRIBE.Content-Type: Response header, typically application/sdp when SDP body is present.
ALL.Session: Required in all requests after SETUP has been performed. Not present before SETUP.
PLAY.Range: Optional. Specifies NPT (Normal Play Time) or clock range for playback (e.g., npt=0-).
PAUSE.Range: Optional. Specifies which part of stream to pause.
RECORD.Range: Optional. Specifies recording range.
ALL.User-Agent: Optional. Client identification string.
ALL.Content-Length: Required if message body is present. Specifies byte length of body.
SETUP.Session: Response header only. Server assigns a unique session identifier. Client must echo this in subsequent requests.
REDIRECT.Location: Mandatory. Specifies the new URL for the client to connect to.

status_changes.description: INIT -> INIT via OPTIONS
status_changes.rationale: OPTIONS is a stateless method that can be sent at any time without changing state. The heuristic trace augmentation supports this, and the invariant claim confirms OPTIONS does not change session state.

status_changes.description: INIT -> DESCRIBED via DESCRIBE
status_changes.rationale: DESCRIBE is the first method after OPTIONS in observed sessions, transitioning from INIT to DESCRIBED state. Evidence from LLM Spec Agent confirms DESCRIBE → 200 is observed in all sessions.

status_changes.description: DESCRIBED -> READY via SETUP
status_changes.rationale: SETUP follows DESCRIBE in observed sessions and transitions to READY state. The invariant claim confirms SETUP → 200 transitions to READY state.

status_changes.description: INIT -> READY via SETUP
status_changes.rationale: While SETUP could theoretically be sent directly from INIT, the observed evidence shows DESCRIBE always precedes SETUP. This transition may be possible but is not directly evidenced.

status_changes.description: READY -> PLAYING via PLAY
status_changes.rationale: PLAY requires prior SETUP (READY state) and transitions to PLAYING. Evidence from LLM Spec Agent confirms PLAY → 200 always after SETUP → 200 in all sessions.

status_changes.description: PAUSED -> PLAYING via PLAY
status_changes.rationale: This transition is plausible from RTSP protocol knowledge but the evidence only shows PLAY from READY state. No direct evidence of PAUSED -> PLAYING transition is provided.

status_changes.description: PLAYING -> PAUSED via PAUSE
status_changes.rationale: PAUSE requires PLAYING state. Evidence from LLM Spec Agent shows PAUSE → 200 then PLAY → 200 in Sessions 2 and 5, supporting this transition.

status_changes.description: READY -> CLOSED via TEARDOWN
status_changes.rationale: TEARDOWN can be sent from READY state. Evidence confirms TEARDOWN → 200 always ends the session in all sessions.

status_changes.description: RECORDING -> CLOSED via TEARDOWN
status_changes.rationale: TEARDOWN should logically work from RECORDING state as well, but no direct evidence of RECORDING state or its teardown is provided in the evidence.

status_changes.description: OPTIONS can be sent at any time; does not change session state (INIT remains INIT)
status_changes.rationale: OPTIONS is observed as the first message in all sessions and is a stateless method. The evidence directly supports this invariant.

status_changes.description: DESCRIBE typically precedes SETUP but is not strictly required by the protocol
status_changes.rationale: Evidence shows DESCRIBE → 200 then SETUP → 200 in all sessions. While typical, the protocol may allow SETUP without DESCRIBE in some cases.

status_changes.description: SETUP must precede PLAY, PAUSE, RECORD
status_changes.rationale: Evidence confirms SETUP → 200 then PLAY → 200 in all sessions. SETUP establishes the session required for these methods.

status_changes.description: PLAY requires prior SETUP (READY state); transitions to PLAYING state
status_changes.rationale: Evidence confirms PLAY → 200 always after SETUP → 200 in all sessions, consistent with READY -> PLAYING transition.

status_changes.description: PAUSE requires PLAYING state; transitions back to READY state
status_changes.rationale: The claim says PAUSE transitions back to READY state, but the transition claims show PLAYING -> PAUSED via PAUSE (not READY). The evidence mentions PAUSE → 200 then PLAY → 200, but the target state after PAUSE is PAUSED, not READY. This contradicts the invariant description.

status_changes.description: TEARDOWN terminates the session; can be sent from READY or PLAYING state; transitions to INIT
status_changes.rationale: Evidence confirms TEARDOWN → 200 always ends the session. Transition claims support TEARDOWN from READY and PLAYING states.

status_changes.description: GET_PARAMETER can be sent at any time, including during PLAYING state
status_changes.rationale: Evidence shows GET_PARAMETER → 200 during PLAYING (Session 3) and during READY (Session 6), supporting the claim.

status_changes.description: DESCRIBE may fail with 404 and be retried successfully
status_changes.rationale: Evidence shows DESCRIBE → 404 then DESCRIBE → 200 in Sessions 3 and 6, directly supporting this invariant.

status_changes.description: Session header is required in all requests after SETUP has been performed
status_changes.rationale: Evidence from LLM Spec Agent field analysis confirms Session header is required in PLAY, PAUSE, TEARDOWN, RECORD requests.
